stem: For $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le360^{\circ}$, the graph of $y=a\cos\theta+q$ passes through the point $A(90^{\circ}, {=q})$ and has its lowest point at $B(180^{\circ}, {=bot})$. Calculate the values of $a$ (the amplitude of the graph) and $q$ (the vertical shift of the graph). Write your answer as $a=\ldots$ and $q=\ldots$.
solution: For an unshifted cosine graph $y=a\cos\theta$, the point at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ has $y=0$, because $\cos 90^{\circ}=0$.
Point $A$ is at $(90^{\circ}, {=q})$, where an unshifted graph would have $y=0$. So the vertical shift is $q={=q}$.
The line $y={=q}$ is therefore the middle of the graph. The lowest point $B$ is at $y={=bot}$.
The distance from the middle of the graph to its bottom is the amplitude: $a={=q}-{=paren(bot)}={=a}$.
notes: Generalises book ex6-8-33 (and ex6-6-4): the point at 90 degrees gives q because cos 90 degrees = 0, and the distance from that middle line to the lowest point at 180 degrees gives a. The book only prints q = 0; here q runs from -4 to 4 (0 included, which reproduces the book case). 'Lowest point at 180 degrees' fixes a > 0, so 'amplitude' is correct wording. The stem does not say that A lies on the middle line: the student is meant to see that from cos 90 degrees = 0, as the book's solution does. Whole numbers only; lowest value ranges from -9 to 3.
